_comment: HAND-CURATED project/news list. Not derivable from the CEEDC data, and deliberately
NOT auto-refreshed: this repo has no backend, and a scraped news feed would rot
silently. Each entry is dated, sourced and checked by hand; `checked` records when.
Scope rule: entries must be real Canadian district energy systems or system changes
with a named operator and a citable source. No vendor press-release puffery, no
The CEEDC dataset already carries 13 systems with status='Planned' and 3 with
status='Decommissioned'. Those come through the pipeline from the data itself and
are NOT duplicated here — this file is for what happened after CEEDC's 2023 cutoff,
or for context the inventory does not record.

projects.name: National Capital Region District Energy System
projects.operator: Public Services and Procurement Canada / Innovate Energy
projects.headline: Canada's federal campus finished converting from steam to low-temperature hot water
projects.body: The modernized NCR DES launched on 2026-06-23, delivered through the Energy Services Acquisition Program as a 35-year public-private partnership with Innovate Energy (PCL Constructors Canada, PCL Investments Canada, EQUANS Services and Black & McDonald). It replaces high-temperature steam distribution with a low-temperature hot water system and electric chillers across four energy centres — Tunney's Pasture, Cliff, Gatineau and the modernized Confederation Heights — plus two pump houses, serving federal and non-federal buildings on both sides of the Ottawa River. It is designed for future connections from other levels of government and the private sector. The launch was marked during IDEA2026 in Ottawa.
projects.why_it_matters: This is the clearest Canadian example of the steam-to-hot-water conversion that 22% of CEEDC's surveyed operators said they were considering — at the largest scale in the country, and postdating the inventory that records it as a steam system.

projects.name: Deep Lake Water Cooling — fourth intake
projects.operator: Enwave Energy Corporation, with Toronto Water
projects.headline: The world's largest lake-source cooling system added a fourth intake
projects.body: Enwave's Deep Lake Water Cooling system draws cold water from Lake Ontario to cool roughly 180 downtown Toronto buildings. A fourth intake pipe added 18 MW, taking base-load capacity to about 60 MW. The City of Toronto and Enwave have since assessed a further expansion, with the preferred option adding up to two more deep intakes at the Island Water Treatment Plant; Enwave anticipates roughly a 35% increase in customer cooling demand. The same infrastructure underpins Enwave's Green Heat program, which supplies low-carbon heat into the downtown district energy grid as part of the city's TransformTO strategy.
projects.why_it_matters: Cooling is the quietest third of Canadian district energy — 981 MW installed against 5,014 MW of heating — and this is the single largest cooling asset in the country.

projects.name: False Creek Neighbourhood Energy Utility
projects.headline: North America's first district network to recover heat from raw sewage
projects.body: Commissioned for the 2010 Olympic Village, the False Creek NEU uses heat pumps to lift waste heat out of raw sewage for space heating and hot water. It has grown more than 300% since it opened, now draws about 70% of its energy from renewable sources — mostly sewage heat recovery — and targets 100% renewable by 2030. Council approved expansion to Mount Pleasant, Northeast False Creek and the False Creek Flats in 2018, and a further project is connecting Vancouver's River District to a new low-carbon source.
projects.why_it_matters: Heat recovery appears in only 5 of 238 operating systems in the CEEDC inventory, yet 59% of surveyed operators named it as a decarbonization option they are considering. This is the Canadian proof case.
